_readme: HiBob's own careers product. Unusually, this platform profile currently has exactly ONE customer - HiBob itself, which dogfoods its own hiring product. It is still written as a platform rather than folded into a standalone profile because the shape is a product's shape, not a company's: any other HiBob customer using the hosted careers site would differ only in subdomain.

israel_filter._note: VERIFIED live 2026-08-13. post_fetch per SKILL Step 5. The response DOES carry a filterGroups.sites list including an 'IL' entry, so a server-side filter appears to exist - but the single call already returns every posting, so filtering client-side costs nothing extra and avoids depending on a parameter whose name was never verified. `country` is the field checked, NOT `site`: site carries a two-letter code ('IL') and country carries the full name ('Israel'). Two-letter codes must not become relevance keywords - 'il' is far too short to match safely against arbitrary location text.

api._note: The listing carries NO per-posting link field - only a UUID id - so the job URL is built from job_url_template, which is why that key exists here and on no other platform. `url` in the field map is a placeholder for schema compliance and is not read by the handler. The template is verified: the ids returned by the API match the /jobs/<uuid> links published on the company's own careers page. NOTE the template embeds this customer's subdomain, so a second HiBob customer would have to override it.

detail_fetch._note:
VERIFIED live 2026-08-13 against the posting above ('Integration Engineer'). inline_field is `requirements` and NOT `description`, chosen the way SKILL Step 3c.1 requires - by reading the actual values rather than taking the first non-empty field. `description` holds the company boilerplate and the role summary; `requirements` is the separate field carrying the qualification bullets. Measured across the 17 Israel-relevant postings: requirements yielded a years-of-experience number on 2, description on 0, responsibilities on 0, benefits on 0. inline_prefix is what makes this field usable at all, and it is not cosmetic. The field arrives as bare '
  • ...' with NO heading, and experience.classify_block decides what a bullet means from the heading above it - so unheaded bullets are never classified as requirements. Prepending a synthetic '

    Requirements

    ' took the same content from 2/17 to 17/17. The text was always there; only the signal that it was requirements text was missing. This is safe here precisely because the field IS the requirements section - applying the same prefix to a mixed description field would promote nice-to-haves into hard requirements and start suppressing jobs the user should see.

health._note: Overridden per company - see the same note in comeet.json.

notes: Endpoint template: https://<tenant>.careers.hibob.com/api/job-ad. One call, everything in `jobAdDetails`, no pagination parameter of any kind observed. THE REFERER HEADER IS REQUIRED: the endpoint returns HTTP 401 to a plain request and 200 to the same URL with a browser-like User-Agent and a Referer of the site's own origin. No cookie or token is involved, so this is a soft anti-scraping check rather than authentication - but it is the most likely thing about this platform to break, and if it is tightened the fetch returns 401, which surfaces as an ordinary fetch failure and reaches a maintenance alert after two consecutive runs. fetchers/api.fetch_hibob derives the Referer from the endpoint so the two cannot drift apart. This platform was added for a single company; the justification is that HiBob runs its own hiring product so there is no third-party ATS to point at, and it contributes 17 Israeli roles, more than most companies in this project's corpus.
